newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian domestic cattle prices ease - CCA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian domestic cattle prices ease - CCA.

text.p: Australian domestic saleyard cattle prices have eased, following their steady recovery since May, because of a fall in export prices, the Cattle Council of Australia (CCA) said on Monday.

October slaughter figures for Queensland and New South Wales were down by 10 percent and eight percent respectively on September, reflecting supply interruptions by rains and seasonal fall in supply in the north, it said in its national cattle market bulletin.

An early start to the wet season in northern Australia brought above average rain to most of the Cape York Peninsula, central Queensland and the northern half of Western Australia and Northern Territory, it said.
A recovery in Japanese consumer confidence and trade activity had seen export and wholesale prices for Australian beef steadily rise, it said.
Rising Australian exports in October included increased shipments to the U.S., Japan, South Korea, Canada, other Asian markets and Mexico, it said.
The U.S. supply situation was one of contrast.
The cow kill increased further in October, maintaining herd liquidation. But fed cattle slaughter remained down as recent increased placements on feed were yet to hit the market, it said.
Australia continued to fare well in recent Korean tenders including the first tender announced against the 1997 quota, it said.
Live exports were heading towards the strongest trading year on record, with exports for the year to September up by 53 percent to 554,352 head.
Feedlot utilisation was expected to rise in the December quarter, the first rise for more than 12 months, it said.
This followed further improvement in grainfed prices from Japan and falls in feed costs.
